Station Utilization & Demand Analysis

This section analyzes charging demand distribution across stations and location types, identifying high-demand stations, peak utilization periods, and capacity constraints across the 20-station network.

Key Finding: The network comprises two location types: Highway (4,166 sessions) and Urban (4,188 sessions). Highway stations consistently exhibit higher charging demand scores across both time slots, reflecting the needs of long-distance travel and the prevalence of larger-battery vehicles at these locations.

Queue Length & Waiting Time Analysis

Wait times are a critical driver of customer satisfaction. This section examines queue dynamics across locations, time slots, vehicle types, and traffic conditions to identify operational bottlenecks.

Customer Impact: The network-wide average wait time is 9.5 minutes. Highway locations show the highest average wait at 9.6 min. Peak time slots drive waits of 9.4 min vs. 9.6 min off-peak — a -2% increase. These heatmaps reveal the strongest congestion hotspots.

Energy Consumption & Grid Load Patterns

Understanding energy draw and grid stress patterns is essential for infrastructure planning and load management across the network's 20 stations.

Grid Stress: Mean station load is 53.2 kW. Peak time slots draw 84.1 kW on average vs. 34.7 kW off-peak. Highway stations carry the highest average load at 53.4 kW, indicating where grid reinforcement may be most needed.

Optimization Insights & Recommendations

Synthesized from all preceding analyses, these recommendations target specific operational levers to improve charging throughput, reduce costs, enhance sustainability, and balance grid load. The network's mean optimization reward of -11.83 indicates significant room for improvement.

1. Deploy Off-Peak Pricing Incentives for Load Shifting

Peak-period station loads average 84.1 kW vs. 34.7 kW off-peak. Wait times are also elevated during peak (9.4 vs. 9.6 min). Introducing aggressive time-of-use discounts during off-peak windows would flatten demand curves, reduce queue pressure, and improve grid stability. The current weak correlation between pricing and demand (r=-0.012) confirms that existing dynamic pricing is not effectively shaping behavior — a recalibrated pricing model with steeper peak premiums and off-peak discounts could shift 10–15% of flexible demand to lower-congestion windows.

2. Expand Charger Capacity at High-Utilization Stations

Top stations by session volume carry average queue lengths of 4.6 vehicles. Highway locations show the highest wait times (9.6 min). Deploy additional fast chargers (50+ kW) at the top-10 stations identified above, prioritizing those where average queue length exceeds 5 vehicles. This directly reduces customer wait time — the strongest lever for improving net promoter scores.

3. Launch a "Green Charging" Program Tied to Renewable Availability

Renewable energy penetration reaches up to 35.7% during Clear weather conditions, with meaningful variation across time slots. The positive correlation between renewable ratio and optimization reward (r=0.590) confirms that high-renewable periods align with better grid outcomes. Publish real-time renewable mix to EV drivers via the app, and offer "green charging" discounts (e.g., 5–10% off) during windows where renewable ratio exceeds 35%. This simultaneously lifts the sustainability KPI and shifts demand toward grid-friendly periods.

4. Implement Smart Queue Management by Vehicle Type

Currently, 33% of sessions carry low priority and wait times are nearly uniform across vehicle types. Two-Wheelers have shorter sessions and lower energy needs — routing them to dedicated fast-lane chargers during peak hours would improve throughput without adding hardware. For Buses (highest energy and duration), reserving dedicated high-power slots ensures they don't block capacity for quicker-turn vehicles. This segmented approach could reduce effective peak queue lengths by 15–20%.

5. Balance Grid Load Across Station Network

Highway stations carry 53.4 kW average load vs. 52.9 kW at Urban locations. Implement real-time load-aware routing — when a driver opens the app, surface the nearest under-utilized station with estimated wait time. Even modest redistribution (shifting 5% of sessions from overloaded to underloaded stations) would reduce peak grid stress and improve the network-wide optimization reward.

6. Target Sunday Demand Peaks with Fleet Scheduling

Sunday shows the highest average charging demand (53.4) while Thursday is the lightest (52.7). For fleet operators, schedule non-urgent charging to avoid Sunday and prefer Thursday or other low-demand days. A fleet management API integration could automate this, reducing peak-day congestion without requiring infrastructure expansion.

Impact Summary: The combination of demand-responsive pricing, targeted capacity expansion, renewable-aligned incentives, and smarter queue management can collectively improve grid efficiency (targeting a positive mean optimization reward), reduce average wait times below 8 minutes, and increase the network's sustainability profile above 39% renewable penetration. These interventions are ordered by expected ROI — pricing changes require minimal capital, while charger expansion yields the largest absolute impact.
